text.la: Dómine, audívi auditiónem tuam, et tímui.
text.en-US: O Lord, I have heard thy hearing, and was afraid.

text.la: Dómine, opus tuum, in médio annórum vivífica illud:
text.en-US: O Lord, thy work, in the midst of the years bring it to life:

text.la: In médio annórum notum fácies: cum irátus fúeris, misericórdiae recordáberis.
text.en-US: In the midst of the years thou shalt make it known: when thou art angry, thou wilt remember mercy.

text.la: Deus ab Austro véniet, et sanctus de monte Pharan:
text.en-US: God will come from the south, and the holy one from mount Pharan:

text.la: Opéruit caelos glória eius: et laudis eius plena est terra.
text.en-US: His glory covered the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise.

text.la: Splendor eius ut lux erit: córnua in mánibus eius:
text.en-US: His brightness shall be as the light: horns are in his hands:

text.la: Ibi abscóndita est fortitúdo eius: (5a) ante fáciem eius ibit mors.
text.en-US: There is his strength hid: (5a) Death shall go before his face.

text.la: Et egrediétur diábolus ante pedes eius. (6a) Stetit, et mensus est terram.
text.en-US: And the devil shall go forth before his feet. (6a) He stood and measured the earth.

text.la: Aspéxit, et dissólvit gentes: et contríti sunt montes saéculi.
text.en-US: He beheld, and melted the nations: and the ancient mountains were crushed to pieces.

text.la: Incurváti sunt colles mundi, ab itinéribus aeternitátis eius.
text.en-US: The hills of the world were bowed down by the journeys of his eternity.

text.la: Pro iniquitáte vidi tentória Aethiópiae, turbabúntur pelles terrae Mádian.
text.en-US: I saw the tents of Ethiopia for their iniquity, the curtains of the land of Madian shall be troubled.

text.la: Numquid in flumínibus irátus es, Dómine? aut in flumínibus furor tuus? vel in mari indignátio tua?
text.en-US: Wast thou angry, O Lord, with the rivers? or was thy wrath upon the rivers? or thy indignation in the sea?

text.la: Qui ascéndes super equos tuos: et quadrígae tuae salvátio.
text.en-US: Who will ride upon thy horses: and thy chariots are salvation.

text.la: Súscitans suscitábis arcum tuum: iuraménta tríbubus quae locútus es.
text.en-US: Thou wilt surely take up thy bow: according to the oaths which thou hast spoken to the tribes.

text.la: Flúvios scindes terrae: † (10a) vidérunt te, et doluérunt montes: gurges aquárum tránsiit.
text.en-US: Thou wilt divide the rivers of the earth. † (10a) The mountains saw thee, and were grieved: the great body of waters passed away.

text.la: Dedit abýssus vocem suam: altitúdo manus suas levávit.
text.en-US: The deep put forth its voice: the deep lifted up its hands.

text.la: Sol, et luna stetérunt in habitáculo suo, in luce sagittárum tuárum, ibunt in splendóre fulgurántis hastae tuae.
text.en-US: The sun and the moon stood still in their habitation, in the light of thy arrows, they shall go in the brightness of thy glittering spear.

text.la: In frémitu conculcábis terram: et in furóre obstupefácies gentes.
text.en-US: In thy anger thou wilt tread the earth under foot: in thy wrath thou wilt astonish the nations.

text.la: Egréssus es in salútem pópuli tui: in salútem cum Christo tuo.
text.en-US: Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people: for salvation with thy Christ.

text.la: Percussísti caput de domo ímpii: denudásti fundaméntum eius usque ad collum.
text.en-US: Thou struckest the head of the house of the wicked: thou hast laid bare his foundation even to the neck.

text.la: Maledixísti sceptris eius, † cápiti bellatórum eius, veniéntibus ut turbo ad dispergéndum me.
text.en-US: Thou hast cursed his sceptres, † the head of his warriors, them that came out as a whirlwind to scatter me.

text.la: Exsultátio eórum sicut eius, qui dévorat páuperem in abscóndito.
text.en-US: Their joy was like that of him that devoureth the poor man in secret.

text.la: Viam fecísti in mari equis tuis, in luto aquárum multárum.
text.en-US: Thou madest a way in the sea for thy horses, in the mud of many waters.

text.la: Audívi, et conturbátus est venter meus: a voce contremuérunt lábia mea.
text.en-US: I have heard and my bowels were troubled: my lips trembled at the voice.

text.la: Ingrediátur putrédo in óssibus meis, et subter me scáteat.
text.en-US: Let rottenness enter into my bones, and swarm under me.

text.la: Ut requiéscam in die tribulatiónis: ut ascéndam ad pópulum accínctum nostrum.
text.en-US: That I may rest in the day of tribulation: that I may go up to our people that are girded.

text.la: Ficus enim non florébit: et non erit germen in víneis.
text.en-US: For the fig tree shall not blossom: and there shall be no spring in the vines.

text.la: Mentiétur opus olívae: et arva non áfferent cibum.
text.en-US: The labour of the olive tree shall fail: and the fields shall yield no food:

text.la: Abscindétur de ovíli pecus: et non erit arméntum in praesépibus.
text.en-US: The flock shall be cut off from the fold, and there shall be no herd in the stalls.

text.la: Ego autem in Dómino gaudébo: et exsultábo in Deo Iesu meo.
text.en-US: But I will rejoice in the Lord: and I will joy in God my Jesus.

text.la: Deus Dóminus fortitúdo mea: et ponet pedes meos quasi cervórum.
text.en-US: The Lord God is my strength: and he will make my feet like the feet of harts:

text.la: Et super excélsa mea dedúcet me victor in psalmis canéntem.
text.en-US: And he the conqueror will lead me upon my high places singing psalms.
